result: direct purchase described as covering virtually all merchandise
notes: The channel that makes the low-margin model possible and its first date is unrecorded - see P1G03.

channel: shipping to a consolidation point and regional cross-docking
date_tested: printed 1994-08-28 and 1995-11-30 about a continuing operation
why_tested: consolidating many small vendor shipments for delivery to warehouses
cost_or_effort: regional cross-dock facilities operated by the company
notes: Earliest date this channel existed on this corpus is 1994; its in-window origin is UNKNOWN.

channel: securing non-prime real estate and refusing elaborate facilities
why_tested: attracting shoppers by price rather than location
cost_or_effort: lower occupancy cost; a conditional-use fight in San Francisco
result: warehouses need not be located on prime commercial real estate sites
repeatability: central to the model and repeated across years
notes: The only in-window documentary trace of the siting doctrine is a city's objections to it.

channel: selling membership through employers and institutions rather than to households
why_tested: reaching qualified buyers through an existing organisation
result: 6.7 million of 10 million memberships were the individual-through-employer class ((PB))
notes: Adapted equivalent of an acquisition channel for this model; its date of first use is a named gap (P1G04).

channel: bundling affordable housing with a retail box to clear a conditional-use hearing
why_tested: needed for a permit in a city protecting neighborhood retail and industrial land
cost_or_effort: 60 to 80 low-income units within the scheme
notes: The one channel fact in this dossier sourced to a document the company did not write.

channel: foreign entry through a 50 percent joint venture
why_tested: market entry outside the U.S. and Canada
result: eight Mexico warehouses by FY1994 period-end
repeatability: accounted on the equity basis so they stay out of the filed estate
notes: Proves the in-window estate numbers understate the operating footprint.

channel: adding ancillary services inside the unit (pharmacy one-hour photo print shop optical food)
why_tested: seeking a margin above merchandise margin
result: added sales cited by the company as a cause of gross margin rising from 9.08 to 9.26 percent of net sales in FY1993
notes: In-window result attributed by the company to a channel whose first date is unrecorded.

channel: direct mail to prospective business members distributed in the period immediately before a new opening
why_tested: recruiting wholesale members where a new unit was about to trade
cost_or_effort: UNKNOWN - no marketing spend is printed for any year
result: sold as standard practice with no measured result
notes: The opening-adjacent half of the recruitment channel. date_tested is UNKNOWN for every channel in this register - which is the finding,  not the gap (U.122).

channel: direct mail to prospective individual members distributed through credit unions and employee associations
why_tested: reaching qualified individuals through an organisation that already had their addresses
result: the individual-through-employer class became the majority of memberships (6.4 million of 9.8 million at 1994-08-28, PB)
notes: The nearest thing this corpus holds to an acquisition-channel mechanism: the distribution medium is another institution's member list.

channel: word of mouth plus payroll-mail follow-up after a base exists
why_tested: lower acquisition cost than paid media
result: the company attributes MOST new memberships to it once a base exists
notes: Unfalsifiable on this corpus: no acquisition-cost figure and no renewal rate exist to test it (U.122,  U.123).

channel: scanning item numbers instead of individually price-marking merchandise
why_tested: allowing price changes without remarking merchandise
result: price changes without re-tagging; substantially all manufacturers supply larger packages pre-marked with item numbers
notes: A supplier-adaptation fact: the channel changed vendors' pack specifications. Earliest date it did so is UNKNOWN.

channel: licensing the concept to an operator in a foreign market
result: a Price Club opened under a licence and its sales never entered the company's series
notes: A fourth ownership mode alongside wholly owned construction, a 60 percent subsidiary and a 50 percent joint venture. Proves the estate series is not the footprint.

channel: acquiring another retailer's site leases rather than a club chain
result: seven locations under a purchase agreement subject to third-party approvals
notes: The only held acquisition of another operator's assets in the corpus - and the only place a rival's property comes to this format. Not a club transaction and no reason for the disposal is printed.

channel: converting non-club real estate into a separately traded company
why_tested: exiting a business not integral to merchandising
cost_or_effort: an estimated 182500 thousand loss on disposal then an 83363 thousand true-up
result: Newco capitalised with 27 million shares and the assumption of certain liabilities
notes: The channel through which the merged company stopped owning its own buildings' surplus - the decision with the only documented alternatives in the archive.
